checks.id: VIS04-§3-D2 (cast-shadow area) — RE-DERIVED, AND THE YAW SWING SURVIVES ITS OWN CONFOUND
checks.value: At the judged window the area is unmoved within the instrument (-0.35% to +0.37%, CHANGING SIGN WITH TAU) and sits at 0.04046 at tau8, above the 0.03 floor. Across the twelve-angle orbit it is BELOW the floor at 2 of 12 (0.02151 at 08:00 yaw 000, 0.02350 at 13:00 yaw 300). I tested the confound the round did not name — `cast_shadow_area_fraction` is normalised by the WHOLE FRAME, so a camera seeing more sky mechanically scores lower. Renormalising by ground fraction (1 - sky_frac, which runs 0.891 to 0.998): the swing is 0.0240 -> 0.1080 at 08:00 and 0.0264 -> 0.1436 at 13:00, i.e. 4.5x and 5.4x. THE SWING SURVIVES; the sky confound accounts for about 8% of it. Between-hour ratio of means is 1.34x against a within-hour yaw swing of 4.9x. THE ROUND'S CORRECTION TO ITS BRIEF IS CONFIRMED: what dominates is where the camera points, not what hour it is.

biggest_gap.what: TWO ROUNDS HAVE TUNED THE AMBIENT AND NEITHER HAS TUNED THE KEY'S HUE, BECAUSE BOTH TOOK ROUND 1'S REMEDY TO MEAN 'WARM' AND WARM IS THE WRONG SIGN. `noon-marsh` declares `keyWarmth: 0.0`. `sky.js:853-854` reads it both ways — positive lerps `sunCol` toward the horizon (warm), NEGATIVE lerps it toward `zen`, which at `day = 1` is (0.115, 0.305, 0.620), a strong blue. Round 1's remedy said start at +0.45. Round 2 measured warm and found it worse (7.16 -> 5.84) and then generalised that to the whole lever class, using a battery whose `cool` term is wired only to the hemisphere and the ambient fill and can never reach the key. Measured by me on the shipped build, pair01, sealed judged crop, my own M6 implementation: control 7.35; ambient colour in either direction 7.30 and 7.37 (inside the 0.22 deg noise floor I measured in the same run); probe x3 6.22 (WORSE, which independently vindicates the round's refusal of the env raise); ambient intensity x4 8.87; and THE KEY RECOLOURED TO THE GAME'S OWN NIGHT BLUE 17.07 — at compensated intensity 17.11, with mean Yp matched to 0.9% lit and 1.8% shadow, `retention` 0.6759, `C_shadow` 8.935 and `C_local_med` unchanged at 0.0245. The best combined arm, blue key with a warm ambient at 4x, reads 16.15 with `retention` 0.7132 and `C_shadow` 10.371 — better than the shipped build on both.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: F4 exists because five blind judges ranked us last of five, twice, and every one of them named the same thing: 'every surface returns the same flat matte olive-grey'. That is a HUE complaint, and `hue_offset` is the corpus's one-number test for it. The round's ruling would have sent round 3 away from lighting entirely and rewritten ring 1's ordering around material differentiation. On this measurement that would have been the wrong call TWICE OVER: the lighting lever is not exhausted, and the one configuration that reaches the bar costs one number in a file F4 already owns. It is also the cheapest thing on the roadmap — three constants and an intensity compensation against a G-buffer normal target.

remedy.action: IN SOURCE, NOT PAGE-SIDE, because the probe must move with the key. In `game/src/render/sky.js`, give the daytime key a genuinely cool hue and compensate its luminous output so the frame's brightness does not move. Two shapes, either acceptable, and the second is the smaller diff: (1) set `noon-marsh`'s `keyWarmth` NEGATIVE and raise the lerp coefficient at `sky.js:854` (today 0.30, which at keyWarmth -1.0 reaches only (0.7345, 0.7495, 0.7600) — near-neutral, and 21% dimmer, so the coefficient alone is not enough); or (2) give the day end of `sunCol` at `sky.js:849-850` a cool triple directly, in the same style as the horizon triple this round already shipped, WITH `R.key` raised by the reciprocal of the Rec.709 luminance ratio so the key's luminous output is unchanged. Either way the change must reach `bakeEnvironmentProbe`'s `sunColour`, which is exactly why a page-side arm is only an upper bound and this must be measured in source. WHILE YOU ARE IN THE FILE: `moon.castShadow = false` at `sky.js:645` still means the light that carries half the clock cannot cast a shadow — carried forward from S64 as an `inapplicable` that names an absence, unchanged by this round.
remedy.acceptance: AT ALL FIVE JUDGED WINDOWS, NOT ONE — S60 says five and this round did one. Report the sealed judged crop and the full frame for every number (S64). (i) M6 `hue_offset` >= 15 deg on the sealed crop at pair01, pair02 and pair03, and not lower than the shipped build at pair04 and pair05. (ii) S59 PRESERVATION, PAIRED, so the hue cannot be bought with brightness: mean `Yp` on the LIT quartile and on the SHADOW quartile each within +/-3% of the shipped build, at every window. (iii) `retention` >= 0.60, `C_shadow` >= 6 and `C_local_med` not lower than the shipped build's, at every window. (iv) S60 clause (a) `key_off >= 2.0x env_off` ON THE LIT SUBSET, measured INSIDE the new configuration and not inherited, at every window; clause (b) cast-shadow area not falling. (v) THE NOISE FLOOR PUBLISHED WITH THE RESULT (S61): capture the shipped configuration twice in the same process and report the spread, because in my run that spread was 0.22 deg and it is larger than the whole of round 2's crop-domain gain. (vi) The twelve-angle orbit re-shot on the new build, since 4 of 12 angles are currently below the 6 deg hard fail and one configuration passing at one pose is not the feature being present.

secondary_observations.what: THE ROUND'S OWN TOOL CONTAINS SEVEN ARMS IT NEVER FIRED. `f4-r2-light.mjs` defines `SETS.hard` — d0 to d6, `WARM_HARD`/`COOL_HARD`/`mixRaw`, the same levers without the constant-luminance normaliser its own comment says pulls a lerp back toward where it started. No metric file, no status row, no report contains any of their ids. I ran them: 3.31 to 7.30 on the sealed crop, i.e. the round's conclusion about them would have been right — but it declared the lever class exhausted without the evidence, and the same battery is the one that cannot cool the key.

THE HEADLINE ABLATION IS BANKED ONLY IN ITS FULL-FRAME FORM. The sealed-crop figures the status file leads with — 26.33 / 8.10 / 2.18 / 2.04 against a floor of 1.86 — are in none of the twelve banked metric files; the JSONs carry `full` only. They are computed from PNGs under `reports/`, which HAZARDS §9 says never reaches the remote. I reproduced all five EXACTLY on my own code from those PNGs while they still exist, and banked the result, so the round's headline is now reproducible off this box. It was not before.

TWO BANKED FRAMES CALLED `AFTER-r2` ARE DIFFERENT ARMS. `frames/AFTER-r2__pair01-crop.png` measures 7.27 on my instrument — it is the REFUSED `env 0.55` arm, a configuration that is not in the tree. `frames/pair01__AFTER-r2__judged-crop.png` measures 7.34 — that one is the shipped build. Nothing in the names distinguishes them. Same family as HAZARDS §17: a verdict's cited artefacts must mean what they say.

THE 'NIGHT IS UNTOUCHED' CLAIM OVERREACHES BY ABOUT ONE HOUR A DAY, AND THE MAGNITUDE IS NEGLIGIBLE. `day = clamp(elev*1.6 + 0.28)` is 0 only for `h` outside (5.33, 18.67), while `night-moon` holds `h` in (18.18, 5.82). So roughly an hour a day of `night-moon` has `day > 0` and the edit does reach it — at the boundary, <= 0.005 in the ambient's blue channel after the `regionNight` lerp. The MEASURED window at 19:30 sits squarely in the `day = 0` band and is genuinely bit-identical. Recorded as a precision correction, not a defect.

THE ROUND'S INSTRUMENT RESULT IS REAL AND I CAN MAKE IT STRONGER. `LightShadow.intensity` against `shadowMap.enabled = false`: the two forms differ by mean|d|luma 0.3368 at 08:00 and 0.1365 at 13:00, while the SAME configuration re-captured differs by 1.0918 and 0.4460 — 31% of the capture's own noise at both hours, reproduced exactly on my code. The stronger statement the round did not make: swapping which `base` frame you subtract moves `cast_shadow_area@tau8` by 0.00266 (0.10364 -> 0.10630), FOUR TIMES the 0.00067 between the two ablation forms. THE CHOICE OF BASE FRAME MATTERS MORE THAN THE CHOICE OF ABLATION FORM. This belongs in HAZARDS.md and it makes §3-D2 affordable at breadth on a software renderer.

THE YAW SWING SURVIVES ITS OWN CONFOUND. `cast_shadow_area_fraction` is normalised by the whole frame, so a camera seeing more sky mechanically scores lower — and sky fraction across the orbit runs 0.0021 to 0.1090, which is a 1.12x effect on ground fraction. Renormalised by ground fraction the swing is still 4.5x at 08:00 (0.0240 to 0.1080) and 5.4x at 13:00 (0.0264 to 0.1436), against a between-hour ratio of means of 1.34x. THE ROUND'S CORRECTION TO ITS BRIEF IS CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED: the dominant variable is where the camera points, not what hour it is, and 'why is 08:00 empty' was the wrong question.

CREDIT, AND IT SHOULD BE SAID AS PLAINLY AS THE FAILURES. This round refused a measured gain because it failed the piece's own acceptance by 1.6% at one tau; it put a value back it could not attribute; it falsified two premises its own brief handed it, including the one about the moon, which I re-verified off a live readback and which is exactly right; and it led with the number that damns it. Its light budget is the first per-term ablation this project has ever run and every figure of it reproduces on independent code. My disagreements are with a mechanism narrated from a sound measurement, a preservation clause argued instead of captured, a battery that could not express the lever, and one window of five — not with its arithmetic and not with its candour.

gap_closure.measured_value: hue_offset, sealed judged crop: 7.16 -> 7.32 (the round's figures; mine 7.18 -> 7.34), against the r1 remedy's own interim target of >= 6.0 deg in every daylight window and the item's 15 deg minimum. Full frame 3.75 -> 6.38, which DOES clear the interim 6.0 target and which the round did not report. `retention` 0.6901 -> 0.6926 and `C_shadow` 14.146 -> 12.377 at the judged window, both above their minima; across twelve orbit angles `retention` is below its minimum at 5 and below the hard fail at 1.
gap_closure.acceptance_restated: The r1 remedy asked for three things at THE SAME FIVE JUDGED WINDOWS, paired per S59: hue_offset >= 6.0 everywhere, retention >= 0.60 and C_shadow >= 6 in every window whose cast-shadow area rose, and S60 clause (a) not falling at any window that already passed. It was measured at ONE window. The half that was measured passes there; the other four windows are unmeasured, so the gap is not closed.

corpus_extended.reason: AMENDMENT — ADD ONLY. §2 gains `§2-D2`: enumerate the light budget per light, ON THE VISIBLE RIG, against the capture's own noise floor, before calling any term a lever or ruling one out. Nothing was removed, no threshold was lowered and no number in §2 changed. WHY: §2's DETECT is one number over the whole frame — it says whether the shadow side takes the environment's hue and cannot say WHICH light failed to put it there. Both F4 rounds chose their lever from an argument about the budget rather than a measurement of one, and S60 clause (a) does not close the hole either because it compares the key against the probe and puts the hemisphere and the ambient fill in NEITHER arm. The clause's sharpest requirement is step 1, which has already been got wrong: a scene-wide `traverse` sum is not the rig — 5.0011 against a visible 0.37107 on this build, a 13x error that became the round's headline sentence. Its second requirement is that a term inside the noise floor is `unresolvable AT ITS SHIPPED VALUE` and may never be reported as absent, as 'not a lever', or as evidence about a class of levers.
corpus_extended.note: BOUND, exactly as CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 requires. DETECT and method only: it adds no route to a higher §14 mark and no route to a higher score for any build, and a critic may cite it to WITHHOLD a mark and never to grant one. NOT THE REASON FOR ANY PASS — this verdict's status is FAIL and the FAIL is set by §2's OWN pre-existing DETECT, which predates me; §2-D2 contributes nothing to the score, which is a min. I checked the whole corpus before declaring the hole rather than assuming it: RI-VIS03 M6 defines the metric and no attribution method; RI-VIS04 §2 names the DETECT and no budget; §3-D2 and §3-D3 (added by the r1 critic) cover shadows, not the light budget; ARBITRATION S60 clause (a) is the acceptance that leaves two of the four visible lights out of both arms. Nothing covered this. Overturned if a visible-chain census proves unavailable to a harness, in which case §2 records the budget UNVERIFIED, which counts as absent.

method_deviations.deviation: I READ THE BUILDER'S STATUS FILE BEFORE CAPTURING, because my brief handed it to me and told me to read it first. CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8 asks for the reverse order.
method_deviations.why: Mitigation, such as it is: my instrument is my own, written from the reference item's pseudocode without opening the one both prior rounds used; my battery was designed from what the round's TOOL could not express rather than from what its status file said; and the two findings that most cut against the round — the visible-rig census and the cool-key arm — came from re-measuring things I had been told were settled. RI-VIS04 declares `blind_pair: no`, so no blind pack was compromised by the ordering.

method_deviations.deviation: I DID NOT FILL §14's THIRTEEN-FEATURE TABLE, and I scored rows 2 and 3 only.
method_deviations.why: F4 moves rows 2, 3 and (untested) 12. A full fill is the joint job of F1/F2/F5/F9, and a critic of F4 alone marking eleven features UNVERIFIED would be reporting on other pieces' work. RI-VIS04 is therefore scored `partial` with `native_score: null`, exactly as round 1 did.

method_deviations.deviation: I MEASURED ONE JUDGED WINDOW, pair01, AND SO DID THE ROUND. S60 names five.
method_deviations.why: The round's entire acceptance table, its light budget, its M6 before/after and its candidate battery are all pair01. Reproducing four more windows across three source arms was not reachable in this session at roughly 60-75 s per 1920x1080 capture under SwiftShader with the box at load 17. I have recorded the shortfall as a FINDING against the round rather than repeating it silently, and the remedy's acceptance names all five.

method_deviations.deviation: MY KEY-HUE ARMS ARE PAGE-SIDE AND ARE AN UPPER BOUND ON THE SOURCE CHANGE.
method_deviations.why: `bakeEnvironmentProbe()` consumes the `uSunColour` UNIFORM, which a page-side light recolour does not touch, so in source a bluer key would also blue the probe's sun lobe and pull the two quartiles back together. I first wrote in my own tool header that this made the arm a LOWER bound, realised the sign was inverted, and corrected the file before filing. It is why this verdict reports the round's ruling as NOT SUSTAINED rather than as OVERTURNED, and why the remedy insists on a source arm.

method_deviations.deviation: EVERY CAPTURE OF MINE IS SOFTWARE (SwiftShader). No hardware confirmation of any window.
method_deviations.why: No Pod available. Every claim here is a differential within one process at one pose, and the run carries its own noise floor (a control re-capture taken after every other arm) so that a movement smaller than the floor is reported as unresolved rather than as an effect.

arbitration_questions.question: S60 clause (a) compares the KEY against the PROBE and puts the hemisphere and the ambient fill in NEITHER arm. Measured on this build's VISIBLE rig, that is 0.558 of ambient intensity (hemisphere 0.37107 + ambient 0.18693) inside no arm of the piece's own acceptance — and the ablation shows both terms are inside the capture's noise floor AT THOSE VALUES while being worth +1.52 deg of hue_offset at 4x. I have added `RI-VIS04` §2-D2 as a DETECT requiring the whole visible budget be enumerated, which is ADD-only and can only withhold a mark. But S60 is arbitration and a critic may not amend it. Should clause (a)'s denominator be ALL non-key light — probe plus hemisphere plus fill — rather than the probe alone?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: not applicable — this is a measurement-domain question inside the FIDELITY axis, not a Souls/Morrowind seam.

arbitration_questions.question: The round measured ONE of S60's five judged windows and reported `clause (a) PASSES`. S64 fixed the DOMAIN (the sealed judged crop) and did not speak to the COUNT. Round 1 failed clause (a) at 4 of 5. Is a single-window measurement of a five-window acceptance reportable as a pass of that clause at all, or must it be recorded `unmeasured` for the other four and the acceptance therefore NOT MET? I have ruled the latter, fail-closed, and scored it that way.
arbitration_questions.souls_side: not applicable — measurement scope, not a design seam.

what_would_make_this_verdict_wrong: MY KEY-HUE ARMS ARE PAGE-SIDE AND OVERSTATE THE SOURCE CHANGE. `bakeEnvironmentProbe()` bakes from the `uSunColour` uniform, not from the light, so a source key recolour would also blue the probe's sun lobe and pull the shadow quartile toward the lit one. If that term dominates, 17.11 could collapse back toward 7 in source and the round's ruling would be right after all. I have said this in the ruling paragraph, in the remedy and here, and it is the single cheapest way to falsify me: one source arm.

MY M6 IS MINE, LIKE THE r1 CRITIC'S BEFORE IT. I transcribed M2/M6/M7 from RI-VIS03's pseudocode and the SKY_MASK step needs a gradient threshold and a connected-component rule that the item states loosely. Two things argue it is sound: it reproduces the round's figures on the same frames to within 0.02 deg on our crops and to within 0.9 deg on three vendored plates spanning 12 to 96 deg, and it was written without reading the implementation it agrees with. A third implementation is the cheap way to falsify me.

MY NOISE FLOOR IS ONE PAIR. The 0.22 deg control-recapture spread that makes me call the round's crop gain `unresolved` under S61 is a single before/after pair. S61 asks for a per-screen band measured by perturbation, and one pair is the weakest form of that. It cuts both ways honestly: if the true floor is smaller, the round's +0.16 becomes a real if tiny gain; if larger, more of the candidate battery is noise.
SOFTWARE RENDERING. Every capture is SwiftShader. Absolute appearance claims would be void; every claim here is a differential within one process.
I MEASURED ONE JUDGED WINDOW. If pair02-pair05 behave differently under the key-hue arm, the remedy's acceptance is the thing that catches it, and it names all five for exactly that reason.

notes.what_the_frames_show: Open `frames/x0-control.png` and `frames/x1-moonkey.png` side by side. The control is what the owner sees today at 08:00 in Lilmoth: a warm-white sun on an olive ground under a pale blue sky, with the lit and shadowed faces of the same stilt-house separated by BRIGHTNESS and almost nothing else — the two hue quartiles sit 7.35 deg apart in Lab, which is the number the corpus calls 'one light source only' territory. In the moon-key frame the shadowed faces go blue against a ground the sun still reads warm on, and the quartiles sit 17.07 deg apart. That is the difference between a frame lit by one lamp and a frame standing in a place, and it is the thing five blind judges named in words.
notes.on_the_round_that_produced_this: The most useful thing this round did is not the change it shipped. It is the ablation — the first time anyone here has switched off one light at a time and reported it against the run's own noise — and the equivalence proof that makes §3-D2 affordable. Both survive independent recomputation. The ruling attached to them does not, and the reason is instructive rather than careless: the round measured everything it could reach and then generalised from a battery it had not noticed was one-sided. That is the same shape as S58, S60 and S63 — a sound measurement with an invented mechanism attached — and it is worth saying that this builder is the one who spotted the same defect in someone else's premise twice in the same session.
